title: A diary of pours
summary: To learn across time, keep a short diary, then read it backward.

cards.text:
Each moment of water has to be remembered
if a later mistake is allowed to blame an early pour.

A longer diary teaches longer gaps.
It also costs more memory.

question.prompt: Throwing away the diary after every moment means…
choices: a late mistake cannot see the first pour
question.simpler: No diary, no lesson across time.

question.prompt: Resetting the water between pictures stops one picture from leaking into the next.
question.why: Each picture deserves its own bucket.
question.simpler: In snnTorch that bookkeeping is utils.reset.

recall.question: Why does a longer diary cost more?
recall.answer: You have to store every moment until the lesson reads backward.

deeper.note: The Python loop over time is the diary. Eshraghian and colleagues walk through it. Tutorial 5 is the companion.

paper.title: Training Spiking Neural Networks Using Lessons From Deep Learning

terms.definition: Learning by storing each timestep and sending the lesson back through that unroll.
